messages.content:
Policy: Protected Health Information
Definition: No person-identifiable data may be input to public AI tools. No business-sensitive or confidential data processing is allowed. Combined details of a local area, a rare disease, and a very young age may enable a patient to be identified, requiring careful anonymisation assessment.
Policy Type: B

Candidate risks:
- 1: Data usage rights restrictions — Terms of service, license compliance, or other IP issues may restrict the ability to use certain data for building models. (Concern: Laws and regulations concerning the use of data to train AI are unsettled and can vary from country to country, which creates challenges in the development of models.)
  Cross-mappings: llm032025-supply-chain[broad], nist-data-privacy[broad], nist-value-chain-and-component-integration[broad]
- 2: Compromise of privacy by obtaining, leaking or correctly inferring sensitive information — AI systems that memorize and leak sensitive personal data or infer private information about individuals without their consent. Unexpected or unauthorized sharing of data and information can compromise user expectation of privacy, assist identity theft, or loss of confidential intellectual property.
  Cross-mappings: credo-risk-036[close], ail-intellectual-property[related], ail-nonviolent-crimes[related]
- 3: Compromised personally identifiable information (Slattery et al., 2024) — The AI system may expose personally identifiable information (PII), either inadvertently or due to adversarial inputs, derived from training data, accessible data, or inferences. PII is any data that can be used to directly identify or contact a specific individual, either alone or in combination with other information.
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-risk-subdomain-2.1[close], ail-privacy[related], ail-specialized-advice[related]
- 4: Personal information in data — Inclusion or presence of personal identifiable information (PII) and sensitive personal information (SPI) in the data used for training or fine tuning the model might result in unwanted disclosure of that information. (Concern: If not properly developed to protect sensitive data, the model might expose personal information in the generated output.  Additionally, personal, or sensitive data must be reviewed and handled in accordance with privacy laws and regulations.)
  Cross-mappings: nist-data-privacy[broad], ail-privacy[related], llm022025-sensitive-information-disclosure[related]
- 5: Data usage restrictions — Laws and other restrictions can limit or prohibit the use of some data for specific AI use cases. (Concern: Data usage restrictions can impact the availability of the data required for training an AI model and can lead to poorly represented data.)
  Cross-mappings: mit-ai-causal-risk-entity-human[related], mit-ai-causal-risk-intent-unintentional[related], mit-ai-causal-risk-timing-pre-deployment[related]

matched_risks.justification: Directly addresses the risk of leaking or inferring sensitive health information.
Relates to the exposure of personally identifiable information, which is a concern in health data.
Concerns the presence of PII in training data, relevant to health information anonymization.
